aquatic-terrestrial insect subsidies are a major source of energy for riparian food webs and that stable isotope analysis is a valuable method to assess the ecological relevance of these subsidies.
the aquatic insect emergence provides a considerable energy and contaminant subsidy to riparian systems.
the aquatic insect emergence provides a considerable energy input to riparian food chains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an ecologically relevant test design for the assessment of the ecological effects of chemicals in aquatic-terrestrial systems, which is based on a mesocosm approach.
the development of an ecotoxicological testing system that allows a comprehensive assessment of potential contaminant effects on aquatic-territional subsidies and riparian food webs.
the development of a new test design for ecotoxicological mesocoms that can be used to study the effects of environmental chemicals and other stressors on aquatic-terstitial subsidies.

the aquatic-terrestrial subsidy of merolimnion-insects may be an important factor in ecotoxicological testing of riparian food chains.

the aquatic-terrestrial subsidy is an important factor in the riparian food webs and that the emergence-related pollutant effects on aquatic insects can be transferred to the terrestrial food web via this subsidy.
aquatic-terrestrial linkages are a key factor to be considered when assessing the effects of environmental pollutants.

the stable isotope ratios of T. extansa and its prey species were affected by the presence of the pollutant and the pollutant’s concentration.

the utilization of stable isotopes can provide a comprehensive and detailed approach for the assessment of pollutant transfer or effects from aquatic to terrestrial systems.
